title: Traditional ANZAC Biscuits
description: A classic Australian favourite — golden, chewy, and steeped in history. This version uses a higher oat-to-coconut ratio for better binding and a less greasy dough. Weigh each ball to 35g for consistent results every time.

youWillNeed.note: Weigh each portion to 35g — bake time depends on size. Inconsistent balls mean inconsistent results.

method.instruction: Preheat oven to 150°C. Line baking trays with baking paper.
Combine flour, oats, coconut, brown sugar, and caster sugar in a large bowl.
In a small saucepan, melt butter, golden syrup, and water over low heat until butter is fully melted. Remove from heat.
Stir in bi-carb soda — the mixture will foam up immediately. Work quickly.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined.
Weigh portions to 35g and roll into balls. Note: if using coconut the dough will feel oilier — this is normal. Place on trays 8cm apart and flatten slightly.
Bake for 20 minutes until deep golden brown. For a crunchier biscuit, bake a further 2–3 minutes. Watch closely — they go from golden to burnt quickly.
Cool on trays for 10 minutes — they will be fragile straight from the oven. Transfer to a wire rack. They firm up completely as they cool.

notes.title: Brown Sugar
notes.content: Brown sugar adds moisture and a deeper caramel flavour. The combination of brown and caster sugar gives the perfect balance of chew and crisp.

notes.title: Storage
notes.content: Store in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks — if they last that long.
